title: Visc-Buckle Trial 1
official: Micro-invasive Suprachoroidal Buckling: Phase 1/2a Clinical Trial
summary: A retinal detachment is a vision-threatening condition that most often requires surgical treatment. Retinal detachments occur because a tear or hole forms in the retina through which liquid can penetrate beneath the retina, separating it from its normal position. Though current surgical treatments for retinal detachment are effective, they all have downsides, such as the need for uncomfortable head positioning after surgery, and slow recovery of vision. In this study, the investigators will test a new treatment for retinal detachment. The investigators will use a special needle to inject a gel between the layers of the eye wall to block off the breaks in the retina and heal the detachment. This procedure combines and modifies ideas from existing surgical techniques, but will eventually be less risky and have fewer disadvantages than current treatments.
